_README: A labeled set for the retrieval-quality harness (lyra_memory.store.evaluate).
THIS IS A REGRESSION BASELINE, NOT THE STEP 3 VERIFICATION.
The sheet is explicit: 'Label first, build second. Hand-label a small set
from existing history.db (653 CLI turns) BEFORE writing the pass that
operates on it. Labeling after seeing the output is grading your own work.'
This corpus is authored, and it was authored after the retrieval code was
written. It therefore cannot serve as the quality verification -- it is
exactly the self-grading the sheet warns about. What it IS good for is
catching regressions: run it before and after any retrieval change and the
The real baseline is 20 turns hand-labeled from ~/.lyra history BEFORE the
next retrieval change. See MANUAL.md section 5.

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: the atoms table is the substrate now, one row per turn, and it is permanent

corpus.speaker: lyra
corpus.text: so everything structural hangs off it as a nullable column

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: right, session_id and salience and retrievability are all cold and re-derivable

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: we chose sqlite-vec over faiss because the store has to be one portable file

corpus.speaker: lyra
corpus.text: faiss would have meant a second index to keep in sync with the database

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: the embedding model is all-MiniLM-L6-v2 at 384 dimensions

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: embeddings are about 75 percent of the store, roughly 75 megabytes a year

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: the dream pass used to write a 3000 character essay and that was the memory

corpus.speaker: lyra
corpus.text: and the essay outranked every atom it was summarised from in retrieval

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: one assembled system prompt reached 44486 characters, almost all retrieved episode text

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: retrieval is three paths now: semantic knn, bm25 lexical, and plain recency

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: the semantic path uses a similarity floor, not a rank cutoff

corpus.speaker: lyra
corpus.text: otherwise a near empty store just returns its best garbage every time

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: bm25 is there to catch repo names and filenames that embeddings blur together

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: we fixed the avatar bug in lyra_embodiment/avatar.js on tuesday

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: lyra-voice runs on port 8001 and lyra-listen on 8002

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: kokoro is the default tts engine, coqui xtts is the alternative

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: whisper handles speech to text in the listen service

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: her own turns get down weighted in recall to avoid a style feedback loop

corpus.speaker: lyra
corpus.text: if I retrieve my own phrasing and repeat it I am reading my own output as evidence

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: trait_history is append only and is the source of truth, traits is the materialized view

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: the identity engine must never mutate a trait without a history row in the same transaction

corpus.speaker: lyra
corpus.text: so the trajectory survives even when the endpoint changes

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: candidate dedup was matching on the label which carries almost no signal

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: 70 candidates produced 60 singletons and exactly one promoted trait in three months

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: we embed the description plus the evidence now instead of the label

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: facts are keyed on subject with free form text and no predicate column

corpus.speaker: lyra
corpus.text: most facts are not triples so a predicate vocabulary would be an authored schema

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: supersession in v1 detects a conflict and stops, it never stamps valid_until

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: over supersession silently erases true things, under supersession is just clutter

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: commitments are the difference between having memory and being useful

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: a due date passing means overdue, it never means done

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: segmentation writes gap_since_prev at the same time it creates the session row

corpus.speaker: lyra
corpus.text: so a month with one conversation in it looks different from a continuous month

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: forgetting is demotion not deletion, storage never shrinks, only competition does

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: the outcome unit is the attempt, not the command

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: ten failed test runs then a pass is one success, abandoning is the failure

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: bulk goes to the runs file, the atom is the event plus a pointer

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: source sandbox_read is excluded from dream input entirely

corpus.speaker: lyra
corpus.text: a file on disk must not be able to write to my identity

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: documents produce facts, never traits or persona

corpus.speaker: wilson
corpus.text: wal mode, backup before every cold pass, thirty day retention not seven
